title: Slot-count sacrifice trigger — fix the string misroute
impact: The reader sacrifices a row result (Isolate.exit zero-copy, at the cost of a reader respawn) when its estimated BYTES exceed 256 KB. Exp 245 measured that this asks the wrong question: `SendPort.send`'s cost tracks the MUTABLE flat-list SLOT COUNT (rows x cols), not payload bytes — strings/immutable leaves are shared on send for free. So a result large in bytes but small in slots (a few rows with a big TEXT/BLOB column — base64 blobs, large JSON/text docs) is cheap to send yet gets SACRIFICED, paying a reader respawn for a copy that never happens. Exp 246 routes the decision on slot count (`raw.values.length`) instead: `_shouldSacrifice` = `values.length > sacrificeSlotThreshold` (default 32*1024 = the exact all-integer equivalent of the 256 KB byte threshold at 8 bytes/cell). End-to-end A/B: the misroute shape (4 rows x 100 KB string) stops sacrificing (1.00 -> 0.00 sacrifices/select) and runs **31% faster** (131 -> 91 us) — every such read previously killed+respawned a reader for nothing; every numeric/structural shape (band 40k, large 200k, medium 20k, small) is byte-for-byte the same routing at parity latency. Threshold is measured, not guessed: the ~48k INTRINSIC crossover (exp 245) regressed the 40k-slot band (+12%, sent something that should sacrifice) because end-to-end the send copy is on the worker's critical path (exp 244), so the crossover arrives earlier; 32k = the byte trigger's all-int equivalent restores band parity while keeping the string fix. Slot count is also free (the flat list's length, no per-cell accounting), so the change is a net **simplification**: the byte machinery it replaced — the byte threshold, `RawQueryResult.estimatedBytes`, and the decoder's per-cell `byteEstimate` — was deleted in the same change, having no readers left once routing moved to slot count. That includes exp 236's `transferableBytes` subtraction, since blob size can no longer influence the decision (exp 236's blob-cell TransferableTypedData wrapping itself is unaffected and still ships). The shippable payoff of the send-vs-sacrifice arc (exp 241 confound -> 244 pool -> 245 intrinsic -> 246 fix).
